title: Moderna and Merck's personalized cancer vaccine wins Phase 3 - TCR 08/20/26
description:
Moderna and Merck's individualized mRNA melanoma therapy plus Keytruda cleared both survival endpoints in a 1,137-patient Phase 3, WIRED reconstructed Flock's OS Investigate police engine from 450 of the company's own exposed files across 120,000+ cameras, and OpenAI cut vetted cyber defenders outside the US and Europe from its strongest models and called it an error.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-20-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:52 Personalized mRNA cancer vaccine clears Phase 3
4:02 Flock's OS Investigate identity engine reconstructed
7:22 OpenAI revokes vetted cyber defenders' access
9:49 Data-center backlash turns electoral
13:03 Generalist AI robot learns from one video
15:51 Close

This episode covers the Moderna-Merck neoantigen mRNA cancer vaccine Phase 3 win, Flock Safety's OS Investigate identity engine, OpenAI's revoked Trusted Access cyber program and Helen Toner's warning, the data-center backlash turning electoral in Pennsylvania and Texas, Generalist AI's GEN-1.5 one-video robot learning, and MIT CSAIL's finding that AI image outputs can't be traced to single training data.

The headlining story is a first for individualized neoantigen therapy: an individualized mRNA therapy, manufactured from one patient's own tumor mutations and paired with Keytruda, cleared both recurrence-free and distant-metastasis-free survival endpoints in a 1,137-patient Phase 3 melanoma trial, and the same platform is already in lung, renal, and bladder trials. Against that, the day's friction stories share one seam: WIRED reconstructed Flock's identity-resolution engine from the company's own files after years of denials, OpenAI abruptly locked vetted defenders outside the US and Europe out of its strongest cyber models, and a Republican campaign committee warned candidates that data-center power bills are turning against them as approval of the buildout splits. The generative side runs alongside it: a Generalist AI robot learned a chore from a single video and improvised with a banana when its tool was pulled, an MIT team showed a large model's outputs disperse across thousands of training images with no single one decisive, and Claude designed protein binders that hit 14 of 15 targets. The thread connecting them is the collapse of the scarcity each old system was priced to.
